item.title: 10-Year Outcomes of Initial CTO-PCI vs No CTO-PCI Strategies for Chronic Total Occlusion: The DECISION-CTO Randomized Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Over 10 years, an initial strategy of CTO-PCI was not associated with a significant difference in the primary endpoint or all-cause mortality compared with an initial strategy of no CTO-PCI. However, the wide CIs preclude definitive conclusions regarding the potential benefit or harm of an initial CTO-PCI strategy. (Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation Versus Optimal Medical Treatment in Patients With Chronic Total Occlusion [DECISION-CTO]; NCT01078051; extended follow-up, NCT06908499).

item.title: Association of Plasma D-Dimer and B-Type Natriuretic Peptide Levels with Acute Ischemic Stroke Mechanism, Severity, and Outcome
item.description: CONCLUSION: D-dimer levels were different among stroke subtypes and were associated with stroke severity, END, and mRS. B-type natriuretic peptide was useful for predicting CE, and was associated with stroke severity but not independently with END or mRS.

item.title: Opportunistic Risk Assessment of Major Osteoporotic Fractures from Routine Chest Radiographs Using Deep Learning
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A survival DL model applied to routine chest radiographs identified patients at high fracture risk with discrimination exceeding that of FRAX, with the greatest benefit in patients with osteopenia. As all participants had been referred for densitometry, absolute-risk and case-finding estimates require prospective evaluation in an unselected routine-radiography population. (Funded by the National Research Foundation of Korea and others.).

item.title: Iron-Catalyzed Regioselective Amidation of Pyridines via Zincke Imine Intermediates
item.description: Achieving precise site-selective functionalization of pyridines is highly desirable in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we present an operationally simple iron-catalyzed protocol for accessing C3-amidated pyridines. The reaction harnesses an in situ-generated Fe-acylnitrenoid that interacts with Zincke imines, which serve as temporarily dearomatized forms of pyridines. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope across C2-, C3-, C4-, or disubstituted pyridine substrates. This approach...

item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Anagliptin Added to Metformin and Empagliflozin 10 mg in Korean Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicentre, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase III Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Anagliptin added to metformin and empagliflozin 10 mg provided confirmatory evidence of additional glycaemic efficacy in a separately randomised Korean population, increased glycaemic responder rates and improved estimated β-cell function, with acceptable short-term tolerability.

item.description: Electrochemical two-electron oxygen reduction (2e^(-) ORR) is an attractive alternative route for the production of hydrogen peroxide (H(2)O(2)). Boron (B)-doped carbon materials have been widely investigated for selective H(2)O(2) electrosynthesis. However, the most stable and abundant B configuration in the carbon basal plane shows limited catalytic performance, requiring a strategy to tune it into highly active B sites. item.title: Vitamins C and D in rotator cuff disease and repair: a narrative review of evidence and gaps relevant to older adults
item.description: Rotator cuff disease can impair function and independence in older adults. However, the value of vitamin supplementation in recovery remains uncertain. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, observational, and interventional evidence on vitamins C and D, identified through a structured search of the PubMed and Embase databases. Older adults were defined as adults aged ≥65 years; most clinical cohorts were younger, limiting their direct applicability. Vitamin C supports collagen...

item.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
item.description: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC-HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. item.title: Stature reveals changing patterns of the biological standard of living in Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 y
item.description: Human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health. Reconstructing this indicator allows insights into which types of societies were providing better health and nutrition-also termed the "biological standard of living" in the literature. Yet, archaeological evidence has not previously been assembled on a scale large enough for systematic comparison across premodern Eurasia. We present a dataset of 18,457 stature observations based on 783 sites from Asia and Europe, roughly...

item.title: The use of unilateral biportal endoscopic approach for intradural extramedullary meningioma excision: a technical note
item.description: CONCLUSION: The technical guide, postoperative outcome, and literature review demonstrate the safe and effective excision of an intradural extramedullary meningioma completely endoscopically.

item.title: Full-length β-tubulin sequencing of Trichuris trichiura in South Korea reveals novel variants with a conserved benzimidazole-binding pocket
item.description: CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Korean T. trichiura form a genetically constrained lineage lacking canonical β-tubulin resistance mutations and retaining conserved benzimidazole-binding architecture. The newly identified G308W and A352D substitutions appear structurally neutral under modeled conditions. These findings establish a multilocus baseline for molecular surveillance in post-control settings and underscore the importance of integrating nuclear and structural markers to detect emerging...

item.title: Development of a Learner-Centered Educational Electronic Nursing Record: A Pilot Study
item.description: The ability to use electronic nursing records has become a critical information-processing competency for nurses. However, nursing students continue to encounter educational barriers due to limited exposure to electronic nursing records during clinical practicum. This pilot study developed an educational electronic nursing record (e-ENR) and evaluated its usability. The study was conducted from August 2023 to January 2024. Following the ADDIE model, the e-ENR was designed and implemented using...

item.title: Effect of tricaprin incorporation on remote drug loading and the performance of drug-loaded liposomes
item.description: We previously demonstrated that incorporating tricaprin (TC), a triglyceride containing three C10 saturated fatty acids, into liposomes enhanced the passive encapsulation and retention of a hydrophilic compound via its effect on membrane packing. This study examined whether TC incorporation could improve remote drug loading and retention while maintaining other formulation properties. Given the role of cholesterol (CHOL) in remote loading and the potential benefits of reducing its content, TC...

item.title: Forecasting endodontic outcomes from intraoral radiographs using a deep convolutional neural network
item.description: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a generalized deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model, ApexNet-17, for predicting endodontic outcomes across all tooth types using preoperative periapical radiographs. A dataset comprising 2,603 teeth from two institutions was utilized. Endodontic outcomes were determined based on tooth survival and radiographic periapical health during 1-3 years of follow-up using the periapical index (PAI). A 17-layer DCNN incorporating self-attention, attention...

item.title: Associations between peripheral immune markers and brain morphometry in normal individuals
item.description: Peripheral immune signaling may be associated with brain structure, but evidence in healthy adults remains limited. We conducted a cross-sectional exploratory study to examine associations between circulating immune-marker concentrations and regional cortical morphometry. Structural T1-weighted MRI and peripheral blood samples were obtained from 62 healthcare workers. Cortical volume, surface area, thickness, and mean curvature were extracted for 68 Desikan-Killiany regions using FreeSurfer....

item.title: Neurological recovery and perioperative outcomes after surgery for degenerative cervical myelopathy in older versus younger patients: a propensity score-matched analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Approximately two in five matched older patients reached the adapted severity-specific MCID threshold, with no significant difference from younger patients, although equivalence was not established. Our findings suggest that advanced age alone should not preclude surgery for DCM, but comorbidity and perioperative medical and rehabilitation needs should guide selection and counseling.

item.title: Biochar for sustainable wastewater remediation
item.description: Biochar, produced from industrial and agricultural waste, has evolved from an agricultural soil amendment to an effective and sustainable material for wastewater treatment. Engineered/modified biochar produced using chemical or physical methods possesses a high surface area, porosity, stability, and a variety of surface functional groups and active sites for removing a wide spectrum of organic and inorganic contaminants, including heavy metals, nutrients, and antibiotics. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Injected mADM exhibited concentration-dependent tissue integration. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The RPVDRI was independently associated with polyvascular disease progression and may complement clinical risk assessment in secondary prevention, particularly in scalable or opportunistic settings where comprehensive clinical information is limited.

A site-specific recalibration step is required before application to populations with different recurrence rates.

item.description: Low muscle mass (LMM) is associated with poor outcomes in cancer, but its role in cancer development remains unclear. We examined pre-existing LMM and site-specific cancer incidence. We analyzed 4,441,403 adults who underwent national health screening in 2012. LMM was defined as the lowest sex-specific quartile of the predicted appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI). item.title: S-Nitrosation: A Cysteine-Based Redox Switch Regulating Plant Stress Resilience
item.description: Plants are unable to evade fluctuating environmental conditions and must therefore continuously adapt to a wide range of biotic and abiotic stressors. To perceive and respond to such challenges, plants have evolved sophisticated signaling networks involving a diverse array of plant growth regulators. item.title: Atogepant for the preventive treatment of high-frequency episodic migraine: Subgroup analysis from the ADVANCE and ELEVATE trials
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this post hoc subgroup analysis, atogepant 60 mg once daily showed greater improvements in efficacy and functional outcomes compared with placebo for the preventive treatment of HFEM, including in those with an inadequate response to ≥2 classes of conventional oral non-migraine-specific preventive treatments. These findings suggest atogepant represents an effective and well-tolerated option for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults with HFEM, a population at elevated risk...

item.title: Risk of Clostridioides difficile infection with potassium-competitive acid blockers: A systematic review with restricted quantitative synthesis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Current incidence-based comparative evidence remains limited and does not support a significant increase in CDI risk with P-CABs compared with conventional acid suppressants. In the restricted vonoprazan-versus-PPI comparison, the pooled OR was 1.07 (95% CI, 0.91-1.25). Agent-specific conclusions remain limited.

item.title: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria perspective: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) as a surrogate endpoint
item.description: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) is an ultra-rare, acquired, life-threatening blood disorder that results in uncontrolled complement activity and intravascular hemolysis (IVH). The associated complications include anemia, fatigue, abdominal pain, hemoglobinuria, erectile dysfunction, and thrombosis, among other manifestations; this nonspecific and variable symptomatology complicates diagnosis and assessment. item.title: External validation of an artificial intelligence-based ECG algorithm for the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction: a prospective diagnostic cohort study
item.description: BACKGROUND: A novel artificial intelligence-based electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) model (AiTiA MI v2.00.00) for the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) was developed using data from Korean patients. Its performance in a European population remains unknown.

item.title: Comparison of 12-Month Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Measures between the BVI Isopure Enhanced Monofocal IOL and the AcrySof IQ Monofocal IOL
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: BVI Isopure showed lower patient-reported spectacle dependence at selected distances and time points, whereas AcrySof IQ showed higher mesopic contrast sensitivity without glare at several spatial frequencies. Defocus curves also showed a numerical tendency toward better intermediate performance with BVI Isopure. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered prospective studies.

item.title: Assessing Visual Field Defects in Glaucoma Using the Perceptive Scotoma Finder
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The Perceptive Scotoma Finder demonstrated reproducible, sector-specific detection of established glaucomatous visual field defects and showed moderate agreement with conventional visual field and RNFL measures. These findings support its feasibility and potential as a rapid, low-cost adjunctive tool for glaucoma assessment; however, further evaluation in early glaucoma and screening populations is required.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Compared with successful PCI for CTO, failed PCI for CTO was not associated with a higher long-term risk of all-cause death or myocardial infarction. Adverse clinical characteristics were an independent predictor of adverse clinical outcomes.

item.title: Indoor Air Quality Management for Patients with COPD and IPF: Practical Recommendations Based on Current Standards and Evidence
item.description: CONCLUSION: This framework provides practical, parameter-specific exposure-management references and strategies for patients with COPD and IPF. Prospective studies should assess whether multicomponent IAQ interventions improve exposure and clinically relevant respiratory outcomes.

item.description: With the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) across various industries, accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for end-users. However, stochastic degradation patterns under unpredictable real-world operations pose a fundamental challenge to conventional prognostic models. item.description: Electronic synapses featuring conduction modulation for synaptic weight update play a central role in implementing neuromorphic computing. item.description: Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro-LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact-mediated detachment, which concentrates stress at the perimeter and causes slip and misalignment. item.title: Field-Free Brightening of Dark Excitons in a Two-Dimensional Perovskite by Organic Spacer Fluorination

item.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: A Review in Neuroimaging
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. item.title: Biventricular Reverse Remodeling After Percutaneous Pulmonary Valve Implantation With a Self-Expandable Pulsta Valve in Native Right Ventricular Outflow Tract
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PPVI with a self-expandable Pulsta valve improved RV unloading, effective RV forward flow, LV filling, and exercise capacity despite an unchanged RV ejection fraction.

item.title: Two-dimensional adhesion noise spectroscopy: a CMOS-based, non-invasive modality for real-time cell and tissue monitoring
item.description: Non-invasive monitoring of cellular adhesion and behavior is essential for lab-on-chip systems, yet current electrical and optical approaches require external stimuli or labels. Here we introduce two-dimensional adhesion noise spectroscopy, a fully passive and label-free electrical imaging modality that repurposes the intrinsic thermal voltage noise of the cell-electrode interface as a real-time indicator of cell attachment. item.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Promoter Affection to 5' Untranslated Region Design for Rational Predictive Translational Engineering
item.description: MOTIVATION: Precise gene expression control is fundamental for biological research and synthetic systems. While biophysical models predict transcriptional or translational regulation, they often overlook their potential interplay. Combining these regulations offers synergistic control, but its influence remains incompletely understood.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The association between social media use and suicidal ideation varied across platforms and demographic groups. After adjusting for confounders, only instances of the use of X, Facebook, and TikTok were associated with higher odds of suicidal ideation. item.description: GAD65-reactive antibodies are common in individuals with DRB1*03:01 haplotypes and diabetes, and benefits from GAD65 therapy are linked to DRB1*03:01 genotypes. item.title: Evolution of the Cytochrome P450 Family 4 (CYP4) Subfamilies in Birds
item.description: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) genes form a large and functionally diverse superfamily of heme-thiolate monooxygenases that catalyse the oxidation of endogenous and exogenous compounds. Within this superfamily, CYP4 enzymes primarily act on fatty acids, substrates central to energy metabolism. Sustained flight and long distance migration in birds rely on efficient fatty acid use, making CYP4 a pertinent system for examining how lipid associated functions may vary across avian lineages. item.title: Stepping up from ICS/LABA to FF/UMEC/VI in Patients with Uncontrolled Asthma: Outcomes from the 52-Week PERFORM Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Escalation to FF/UMEC/VI from ICS/LABA improved lung function, asthma control, and clinical remission, with no unexpected safety findings versus usual care ICS/LABA at Weeks 24 and 52, consistent with the overall PERFORM population. Initiation with FF/UMEC/VI may address the unmet need for optimized treatment in patients with uncontrolled, infrequently exacerbating asthma.

item.description: To establish functional seed traits, the accomplishment of proper seed maturation on mother plants is essential. item.title: Targeted degradation of MDM2 by nucleus-directed indirect ubiquitination
item.description: We present an MDM2 degrader that functions through the non-covalent tethering of ubiquitin to MDM2. Chimeric degraders comprising a nuclear localization sequence, M1-linked diubiquitin, and an MDM2-targeting ligand markedly reduced intracellular MDM2 levels, establishing a non-enzymatic platform of targeted ubiquitination that enables fine control of intranuclear protein stability and degradation.

item.description: Symmetry and objectness both play a supporting role in figure-ground organization. Previous work predominantly assessed their interplay using simple black and white stimuli. In this study, we examine the interaction between figure-ground organization and objectness in symmetry detection by analyzing data from a preregistered experiment where participants identified regions of symmetry in natural scenes using a bounding-box method. item.title: Rethinking Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome: Insights Into Diagnosis and Therapeutic Strategies
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Conservative management should be the initial approach in suspected SMA syndrome. Careful diagnosis combined with structured medical therapy can yield clinical benefit while avoiding surgical risks. Prospective studies are needed to refine criteria for intervention.

item.description: Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-to-arachidonic acid (AA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-to-AA ratios (EPA/AA and DHA/AA ratios) in blood are widely recognized as useful indicators of the risk of atherosclerosis. This retrospective cohort study included 479 adhesively treated VRF teeth at Hokkaido University Hospital between 1995 and 2020. item.title: Peanut Allergy in Asian Children: From Regional Epidemiology and Molecular Sensitization to Oral Immunotherapy and Biologics
item.description: Peanut allergy has traditionally been considered less prevalent in Asia than in Western countries, where it is a major cause of food-induced anaphylaxis. Contemporary evidence challenges a uniform low-prevalence model and demonstrates marked geographic and methodological heterogeneity. item.title: Cardiac Rhythm Disorders and Chronic Occupational Exposure to Pollutants: A Systematic Review
item.description: Heart rhythm disorders (arrhythmias) are a growing public health problem and can result from an imbalance in the autonomic nervous system or be exacerbated by lifestyle factors. Recent epidemiological data indicate that certain environmental factors, such as air pollution, can alter cardiac electrophysiological function. item.title: Decoding Complications: Large Language Model-Based Classification of Free-Text Entries in Clinical Stroke Registries
item.description: Clinical registries capture adverse events (AEs) in free-text fields that are rarely analyzed. We developed a reproducible large language model (LLM)-assisted workflow using 11,216 free-text entries from 18,069 patients in the German Stroke Registry; 9,146 informative entries were retained after filtering.
